study_identification_part.si_4_title: Dissecting the Heterogeneous Cortical Anatomy of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Normative Models

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used the Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP) cohort, which is a multi-site dataset collected across six European sites: Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology and Neuroscience, King's College London; Autism Research Centre, University of Cambridge; Radboud University Nijmegen Medical Centre; University Medical Centre Utrecht; Central Institute of Mental Health, Mannheim; and University Campus Bio-Medico, Rome. The LEAP dataset is listed in the dataset table as 'LEAP' (Longitudinal European Autism Project).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "we included all participants from the Longitudinal European Autism Project (40) cohort with a structural magnetic resonance imaging scan surviving quality control and the necessary clinical and demographic data."

answer.LEAP: normative model training/testing (TD subjects) and clinical application (ASD subjects)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The TD participants (n=206) from the LEAP cohort were used for estimating the normative model of cortical thickness development via Gaussian process regression, with 10-fold cross-validation for generalization assessment. The model was then retrained on the full TD dataset and applied to the ASD participants (n=321) to estimate individual deviations from the normative pattern.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "we generated a developmental model of typical brain development by training a Gaussian process regression model on the TD cohort (n = 206) using age and gender as covariates" ... "To assess generalization, we used 10-fold cross-validation before retraining the model using the whole dataset to make predictions on the ASD participants"
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Zabihi2019.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Constructing a Normative Model of CT, L70-L73

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model of cortical thickness was constructed using all 206 TD individuals with Gaussian process regression. 10-fold cross-validation was used to assess generalization (approximately 185 training and 21 test subjects per fold), then the model was retrained on the entire TD cohort (n=206) for final predictions on the ASD cohort. The same approach was also applied to surface area, but the primary model was for cortical thickness.
